offline_1920.caption:
neurons offline — the 1M network runs while he is awake when the GPU is on · static cells, no activity
cells enlarged ~14× for visibility · 2,901 cells (pyramidal, basket, thalamic relay, medium spiny, CA1 pyramidal, amygdala principal; ≤ 40 segments each) · NeuroMorpho.Org, CC BY 4.0 · credits on /about
Shapes are real reconstructed neurons (public databases); thickness, spines and myelin are drawn from published typical values. The simulated network uses point neurons (no dendrites are simulated); cells are enlarged and pulses slowed to be visible. A model, not a mind.

live_1920.caption:
live · 20k-neuron network on CPU · last frame: 5,739 spikes recorded, none sent (the stream's 3 KB/s budget was used up)
cells enlarged ~14× for visibility · 2,901 cells (pyramidal, basket, thalamic relay, medium spiny, CA1 pyramidal, amygdala principal; ≤ 40 segments each) · a spike glows soma → axon, slowed ~250×; region rates tint the dendrites · NeuroMorpho.Org, CC BY 4.0 · credits on /about
Shapes are real reconstructed neurons (public databases); thickness, spines and myelin are drawn from published typical values. The simulated network uses point neurons (no dendrites are simulated); cells are enlarged and pulses slowed to be visible. A model, not a mind.
Simulated spiking neurons (1M on GPU / 20k on CPU) inside the real wiring of one person's brain; each drawn cell stands for a sampled model neuron; a model, not a mind.
